title: form::Field::editable's doc cites a guard that was never written, so a form can offer an edit the store refuses
body:
`form::Field::editable`'s doc names a guard that does not exist, and the guard is the one thing standing between a form declaration and an edit the store refuses.

## The claim

`intentsvcs/src/form.rs:109-117`, on `Field::editable`:

> Whether this realiser offers to edit the row.
>
> **A DECLARATION, NOT AN AUTHORITY.** The mutation surface decides what can actually be written; this says whether the form OFFERS it. A row declaring `true` for a field the surface refuses is a form that invites an edit the store will reject, so `[Loaded::offers_an_edit_the_surface_refuses]` **reports the disagreement rather than letting the realiser discover it after the keystroke.**

## The measurement

`offers_an_edit_the_surface_refuses` appears **exactly once in the whole tree: in that doc comment.** It is an intra-doc link to a method that was never written. `impl Loaded` carries `load` and `from_str` and nothing else.

So the behaviour the comment describes in the present tense -- *reports the disagreement* -- does not happen, and the outcome it contrasts itself against -- *letting the realiser discover it after the keystroke* -- is what actually ships.

## Why it is worth a record rather than a quiet fix

**A doc comment written in the present tense about a mechanism that does not exist is indistinguishable from one describing a mechanism that does.** Nothing goes red; a reader looking for the check finds a name and stops looking. This estate has now caught the same shape three times in a month -- a `render.rs` comment claiming an import that had not been made, `error_remedies.rs`'s exemption list citing a cover that could not fail, and this -- which makes it a class rather than an accident.

**It is load-bearing for `AC-17.1` specifically.** That row requires *an edit made through EACH realiser reaches an identical store state*. Two realisers agreeing about which fields are editable is a precondition for the claim, and `editable` is a per-realiser DECLARATION with no authority behind it. Without the check, the TUI and a browser realiser can each honour the declaration faithfully and still diverge from the store's actual mutation surface -- in the same direction, silently, which is the failure mode hardest to see from either end.

## What is NOT claimed here

That any form CURRENTLY declares `editable: true` for a field the surface refuses. That was not measured; `surface/forms.json` may well be correct today. **The defect is the absent guard, not a present disagreement** -- and a declaration that happens to be right on the day it is written is exactly what the guard exists to keep true afterwards.
